units.passage: Additionally, the use of AI to complete assigned work may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy.
units.why: The sentence says "the use of AI to complete assigned work may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy". It classes AI use on assignments as potential academic misconduct, so P36; it is hedged ('may'), hence informs, and it binds students.

units.passage: With this in mind, remember that representing work that you did not produce as your own, including work generated or materially modified by AI, constitutes academic dishonesty.
units.why: The sentence classes passing off AI-generated or AI-modified work as one's own as 'academic dishonesty'. I chose P36 (classification as misconduct) over P19 because the sentence defines the offence rather than listing a banned use.

units.passage: Use of generative AI in a way that violates an instructor’s articulated policy, or using it to complete coursework in a way not expressly permitted by the faculty member, will be considered a violation of the Honor Code.
units.policy: Using generative AI in a way that violates an instructor's articulated policy is a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: "violates an instructor's articulated policy ... will be considered a violation of the Honor Code": breaking an instructor's AI rule is classed as an Honor Code violation, so P36.

units.passage: Be explicit with students about your expectations regarding the use of ChatGPT and related AI tools for assignments, exams, and in the classroom, and be clear that engaging in unauthorized use of generative AI will be considered a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: Instructors should make clear that 'unauthorized use ... will be considered a violation of the Honor Code': misconduct classification (P36).
